input.quote: CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and indirect damages are mutually excluded, but the only carve-out is Paragraph 9 (independent-contractor/tax obligations) — there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, which the fallback requires. The basis is also fees paid for the specific SOW Services rather than 12 months' fees, which can fall well below six months' fees on a short task-based engagement. Redline sets the 12-month basis, adds an Excluded Claims sentence and confirms our payment obligations sit outside the cap.

input.quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Despite the heading, Section 7 contains no indemnity language at all in either direction, and Section 5(c)'s non-infringement warranty is a bare representation with no defence or indemnity obligation and no remedy. There is no Contractor IP indemnity anywhere in the document, so we have inserted our standard Contractor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a standard procedure.

input.quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
input.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Company; the only "competition" language preserves Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which does not restrict us. We note Section 4(b)(ii) restricts our resale/use of Contractor's own materials, but that is a licence-scope point (addressed under LICENSE), not a restrictive covenant.

input.quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services")
input.rationale: The engagement is expressly task-by-task via Statements of Work with no "sole and exclusive provider" or requirements-purchasing language in Sections 1 or 3, so we retain full freedom to use other suppliers.

input.quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: Section 3 contains no most-favoured-nation mechanic in either direction, so there is no obligation on us to extend Contractor best terms or match third-party offers. Nothing to redline.

input.quote: Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services
input.rationale: This sits at our fallback: mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, 12 months post-termination, and a solicitation (not no-hire) restriction. We note it lacks express carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches — a drafting point we would raise but not a deviation.

input.quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
input.rationale: The term is evergreen (Section 2) but the convenience right is available only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so we have no ability to exit an in-flight engagement — effectively no Customer convenience right, which fails the fallback. Contractor's 15-day convenience notice is also far short of the 90 days we require. Redline gives Company 30 days' convenience termination of the Agreement or any SOW with a prepaid-fee refund and moves Contractor to 90 days.

input.quote: The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
input.rationale: There is no automatic renewal, no renewal term and no non-renewal notice window, so none of the walk-away risks arise; the evergreen term is more favourable to us than a renewing term. We note Section 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap — a price-predictability point we would raise (lesser of CPI and 3%) rather than a renewal deviation.
